purpose: Bounded coupled-determinism development retrieval; separate from the frozen historical development set and held-outs.

questions.query: Are repeated desktop runs of native cells and Rapier bodies bit-identical, and what makes them diverge?
facts: The default independently paced worker prepares whichever body sample main last published; every repeated asynchronous pair diverged by that race.
A default-off lockstep fence (set_lockstep_coupling) plus a main-side frame hold made same-host repeats and 1/4 native workers bit-identical in one fixture; main.gd does not use it.

questions.query: Can Windows and Linux replay the same coupled sand and rigid body simulation bit for bit for multiplayer lockstep?
facts: Not established in production: registered Windows and Linux lockstep runs diverged after a one-ulp float32 rotation difference from Transform2D.get_rotation() packed from bit-identical Rapier transforms; a fixture-only double atan2 repack matched both hosts for 1800 ticks.
The Rapier build enables parallel and lacks enhanced-determinism; cross-platform replay and multiplayer remain Planned/not admitted.

questions.query: How do I enable the lockstep coupling fence and read its holds and timeouts?
facts: set_lockstep_coupling(enabled, hold_timeout_usec=250000) is default off and refused after start_worker; it covers only the ordinary coupling path.
rigid_body_publication(), the snapshot field consumed_rigid_body_publication and lockstep_metrics() expose publications, holds, hold time and timeouts.
